issues.description: The problem statement and tests expect a function named make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None, but the template defines create_y_state(...) instead (and raises a NotImplementedError mentioning make_y_state). The solution implements make_y_state. This name/signature mismatch in the template will confuse students and prevent them from implementing the required function under the expected name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_y_state to make_y_state and ensure its signature matches the problem statement (make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None). Alternatively, add a thin wrapper make_y_state that calls create_y_state, and update the NotImplementedError text to reference the correct function name so students implement the function expected by the tests.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named make_y_state(...) to prepare a noisy |Y> resource state, but the template repository defines the function as create_y_state(...). This mismatch will prevent students from finding/implementing the required function name and will break automated tests that call make_y_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_y_state to make_y_state (and update any internal references and error messages) so the template, problem statement, and solution consistently use make_y_state(...).
